snippet.title: Why Joe Jackson Made His Kids Call Him "Joseph" — Not Dad 🎤💔
snippet.description:
Joe Jackson created the Jackson 5 and guided his children to pop superstardom. But there was an unusual rule at the center of his parenting: none of his children were allowed to call him "Dad" or "Daddy" [citation:1][citation:4][citation:6].

Instead, they had to address him as "Joseph" [citation:1][citation:3][citation:7].

🗝️ WHY HE DID IT:
- To maintain a strict, authoritative distance [citation:1][citation:2]
- To prioritize the manager-father dynamic over a warm parental role [citation:1][citation:4]
- To ensure his children "listened" and stayed out of trouble [citation:2][citation:11]

Both Michael and Janet later expressed how much the rule hurt them. Michael said he wanted to call him "Daddy so bad," and Janet once tried to call him "Dad"—only to be corrected on the spot [citation:1][citation:2].

The stories of his abuse—whippings with belts and switches, verbal threats, and intense rehearsals—paint a picture of a man who valued success over emotional connection [citation:1][citation:3][citation:6].
